comments.content: The test creates a `gemini-extension.json` inside `rig.testDir` and then installs the extension from that same directory. Since `rig.testDir` is also the cwd for the spawned CLI process, the extension's manifest will be picked up as part of the working directory. More importantly, `rig.cleanup()` is only called at the end of the test body; if any assertion fails (e.g. `expect(result).toContain('test-extension')`), cleanup and `rmSync` will be skipped, leaving the installed extension registered globally and polluting subsequent test runs. Wrap the body in try/finally (or use afterEach) so uninstall/cleanup always runs.

`runCommand` writes to `child.stdin` only when `options.stdin` is provided, but never closes stdin otherwise. If the spawned CLI waits on stdin (e.g. prompts for confirmation), the process will hang indefinitely. Consider always calling `child.stdin!.end()` after optionally writing, so the child sees EOF when no input is supplied.

`runCommand` rejects with only `stderr` in the error message. When the CLI exits non-zero but writes diagnostics to stdout (common for CLI tools), the failure message will be empty and hard to debug. Include `stdout` in the rejection message as well.
